newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia on verge of big minerals growth-minister.
newsitem.headline: Australia on verge of big minerals growth-minister.

text.p: Australia was on the verge of a massive upsurge in minerals and energy exploration and development with a staggering A$55 billion worth of projects already being built or under active consideration, Federal Energy and Resources Minister Warwick Parer said on Tuesday.
If only 87 percent of projects got off the ground, the amount of money generated from them would wipe out the nation's current account deficit, Parer told Reuters.
"If ever we were on the edge of great growth in this country, it is right now and all it needs is resoration of investor confidence," he earlier told a business meeting.
Parer said that 20 percent of the world's exploration efforts was still centred on Australia, despite uncertainty being generated by Aboriginal land title issues.
He said he had been told by the mining industry that the biggest issue needing a national solution was the uncertainty faced by miners over the High Court's Wik decision.
In a split decision, the court ruled that native title could co-exist with pastoral leases under certain circumstances, creating a great deal of uncertainty for miners and farmers.
Many mining leases are on existing or former pastoral leases.
However, the mining industry generally supported the Federal government 10-point plan to achieve security of land tenure, Parer said.
He also said Australia was prepared to accept measures to contain global warming but only if the burden was shared.
Australia's contribution to world greenhouse emissions was 1.4 percent compared with 26 percent from the United States and eight percent from Japan, he said.
"We are happy to address it in a fair and equitable way," Parer said.
